function.name: client_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates of a single client based on the client's name and the status of the mandate. Partners can use this API to retrieve mandate information for their clients. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the client whose mandates are to be fetched.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If not specified, mandates with all statuses are retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches all mandates for all clients associated with a partner, filtered by the status of the mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of mandates to fetch. Possible values are 'active', 'pending', and 'inactive'.

function.name: partner_sips
function.description: Fetch all Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs) of all clients associated with a partner, filtered by the given status of the SIP. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the SIPs to be fetched. Valid statuses include 'active', 'stopped', and 'paused'.

message.content:
A **mandate** in financial terms refers to a formal authorization granted by one party (the *principal*—often a client or investor) to another party (the *agent*—such as a broker, fund manager, or bank) to act on its behalf in specific transactions or activities. Key points: | Aspect | Description | |--------|-------------| | **Purpose** | Enables efficient execution of trades, portfolio management, or other services without requiring the principal’s direct involvement each time. | | **Scope** | Can cover buying/selling securities, managing assets, executing orders within set limits, or handling cash flows. | | **Types** | • Active – currently valid and enforceable.
• Pending – awaiting approval/activation.
• Inactive – expired, revoked, or otherwise no longer effective. | | **Common Use Cases** | • Investment funds giving managers discretionary trading authority.
• Clients authorizing brokers to place market or limit orders.
• Corporate treasuries delegating liquidity management to banks. | In practice, a mandate often includes details such as: 1. **Authority Limits:** maximum trade size, risk thresholds, asset classes allowed. 2. **Duration & Conditions:** start/end dates, renewal clauses, performance benchmarks. 3. **Reporting Requirements:** frequency and format of activity reports back to the principal. Understanding whether a mandate is active, pending, or inactive helps partners assess which accounts they can engage with at any moment.
